newsitem.title: UK: Britain cautious over sending soldiers to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Britain cautious over sending soldiers to Zaire.

text.p: Defence minister Michael Portillo said on Monday Britain was unlikely to send troops to eastern Zaire to help humanitarian relief efforts.
Tutsi rebels controlling the area have agreed to open an aid corridor to enable relief workers to reach hundreds of thousands of Hutu refugees trapped by fighting.
Portillo said detailed planning would be needed to ensure any international force that might be sent to Zaire could disengage from the country.
"If there is to be a military operation it must be carefully planned, it must have clear objectives and there must be an exit strategy," Portillo said in a BBC radio interview.
"In other words we must know how forces would withdraw whether those forces are African or non-African."
Asked whether Britain might be involved in such a force, Portillo said Africa was "not exactly Britain's backyard" and added: "I don't think that is the most likely thing."
However, he said: "What I do think is that Britain must be involved in helping to ensure that starving people are saved from starvation if there is anything we can do."
On Friday, Prime Minister John Major said it was "certainly possible" that Britain could send troops to eastern Zaire.
